subtitle: Sindh at the Edge of Two Worlds

panels.shot: split composition, half showing a fortified Sindhi city on the Indus, half a desert army under black banners, both looming toward each other
panels.action: Raja Dahir stands on a high battlement above the Indus while, on the other side of the frame, a youthful Muhammad bin Qasim rides at the head of an advancing desert host, the river and sea between them glowing under a harsh sun.

dialogue.text: In 711, as Sindh’s river ports fed the Indian Ocean and Iraq’s empire reached east, Raja Dahir and Muhammad bin Qasim met in a war that our books remember very differently.

i18n.hi: ७११ में, जब सिंध के नदी-बंदरगाह हिंद महासागर को खिलाते थे और इराक की सल्तनत पूरब तक फैली थी, राजा दाहिर और मुहम्मद बिन क़ासिम की जंग को हमारी किताबें बिल्कुल अलग तरह से सुनाती हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in over a map-like vista of the Indus delta and Arabian Sea lanes
panels.action: A bird’s-eye view reveals the Indus splitting into many channels toward the sea, dotted with harbors and boats, while a faint overlay of caravan trails and distant desert settlements hints at links to the west.

dialogue.text: Before the conquest, lower Sindh was a frontier of worlds: Brahman kings at Aror, Buddhist monasteries by the river, Jat clans in the marshes, merchants tying the Indus to Basra and beyond.

i18n.hi: फ़तह से पहले, निचला सिंध कई दुनिया की हद थी: अरोड़ के ब्राह्मण राजा, नदी किनारे बौद्ध विहार, दलदलों में जाट कबीले, और व्यापारी जो सिंधु को बसरा और आगे से जोड़ते थे।

panels.shot: medium wide interior of a Sindhi court hall
panels.action: Raja Dahir sits on a carved wooden throne in an open pillared hall, Brahman advisers near him, while envoys from port towns and river chiefs stand below, their attire mixing coastal and inland styles.

dialogue.text: Dahir, last of the Brahman rulers of Sindh, held forts and ferries along the Indus. His power ran through tribute, alliances and the control of ports more than through line upon line of soldiers.

i18n.hi: दाहिर, सिंध के आख़िरी ब्राह्मण शासक, ने सिंधु किनारे क़िले और घाट संभाल रखे थे। उसकी ताक़त ज़्यादा कर, सियासी मेल और बंदरगाहों की पकड़ से चलती थी, न कि अंतहीन सिपाही-क़तारों से।

panels.shot: low-angle wide shot of an Umayyad governor’s desert court in Iraq
panels.action: In a stark desert palace courtyard, an Umayyad governor confers with Arab commanders, rolled maps of the eastern frontier on a low table, a black banner stirring behind them in the hot wind.

dialogue.text: Far to the west, the Umayyad caliphate eyed the same seas. From Basra and the new garrison towns, governors pushed east, seeking secure routes, taxes and glory from Baghdad’s predecessor capitals.

i18n.hi: काफ़ी पश्चिम में, उमय्यद ख़िलाफ़त की नज़र भी इन्हीं समंदरों पर थी। बसरा और नए फ़ौजी क़स्बों से सूबेदार पूरब धकेल रहे थे, रास्तों की सुरक्षा, कर और शोहरत ढूंढते, बग़दाद से पहले की राजधानियों के लिए।

panels.shot: tight medium on a youthful commander receiving orders
panels.action: A young Muhammad bin Qasim stands straight as an older governor gestures toward the east on a map, other officers watching; the boyish commander’s face shows both ambition and the weight of expectation.

dialogue.text: Into this frontier walked Muhammad bin Qasim, a teenage commander of an Arab tribal elite. Chosen by his kinsman, the powerful governor Hajjaj, he led not invincible hordes but a disciplined provincial army.

i18n.hi: इसी सरहद पर कदम रखता है मुहम्मद बिन क़ासिम, अरब क़बीलाई अशराफ़ का एक नौजवान सरदार। अपने रिश्तेदार, तगड़े गवर्नर हज्जाज की पसंद से, वो अजेय लश्कर नहीं, बल्कि सधा हुआ सूबाई लश्कर लेकर चला।

panels.shot: wide seascape of Debal’s harbor and fort
panels.action: The coastal city of Debal rises by the sea, its high temple-fort overlooking a busy harbor of sails and masts, while beyond the horizon small Arab warships approach in formation.

dialogue.text: The Arabic chronicles open at Debal, a walled port beneath a tall temple. Sindh's ships were accused of seizing Arab vessels; Hajjaj wanted the route, the plunder and a province.

panels.shot: siege wide shot from behind Arab engines facing Debal’s walls
panels.action: Arab troops work a large stone-thrower aimed at Debal’s walls, while defenders watch from crenellations, some in armor, some in simple cloth, the tension of siege heavy in the air.

dialogue.text: Al-Baladhuri tells of siege engines hauled from Iraq; the Chachnama adds omens and speeches. Both agree Debal was stormed, its fighting men killed, its temple cast down, and captives enslaved and sent west.

panels.shot: medium on Arab envoys and local notables in a tense parley
panels.action: Within a courtyard inside Debal, Arab envoys and local city notables face each other, hands open in talk, their faces guarded; behind the locals, merchants and townsfolk watch anxiously from doorways.

dialogue.text: The terms were plain: those who submitted paid the jizya and kept their lives and trades; those who resisted were stormed. Some towns opened their gates; others did not.

panels.shot: medium shot inside Aror’s court, Dahir receiving news
panels.action: Raja Dahir stands from his throne as a dusty messenger bows deeply, holding a broken city emblem from Debal; courtiers lean in, some alarmed, some calculating.

dialogue.text: News travelled upriver. Debal had fallen. A new power now held a gateway to the sea. For Dahir, it was no longer a distant Arab raid; it was a rival regime planted at his river mouth.

i18n.hi: ख़बर नदी के ऊपर तक पहुंची। देबल गिर चुका था। अब समंदर का एक दरवाज़ा नए हाकिम के हाथ था। दाहिर के लिए ये कोई दूर की अरब लुटेरी टुकड़ी नहीं, बल्कि उसके ही मुहाने पर जड़ जमा चुका एक मुकाबिल निज़ाम था।

panels.shot: wide of Dahir inspecting his forces near Rawar
panels.action: On a dusty plain near the Indus, Dahir rides past lines of armored horsemen, infantry with spears, and elephant corps; beyond them rise the faint outlines of district forts and fields.

dialogue.text: The king gathered his strength near Rawar, south of Aror. His army was no mythic million; it was a regional force, drawing on chiefs, retainers and levies whose loyalty was as political as it was personal.

i18n.hi: राजा ने अपनी ताक़त अरोड़ के दक्षिण, रावर के पास समेटी। उसका लश्कर कोई अफ़सानों वाला लाखों का हुजूम नहीं, बल्कि एक सूबाई फ़ौज थी, जिसमें सरदार, जंगी अनुचर और बुलाए गए सिपाही थे, जिनकी वफ़ादारी जितनी सियासी थी उतनी ही शख़्सी।

panels.shot: wide shot of the opposing armies taking positions by the Indus
panels.action: Two hosts face each other across a flat, open field near a branch of the Indus, Dahir’s elephants and standards on one side, Qasim’s lines of light cavalry and infantry on the other, the sky thick with dust.

dialogue.text: Near Rawar or close to Aror, the sources agree, they met. The Chachnama adorns this field with omens and fiery speeches. Strip them away, and we still see the stark truth: two states vying for the same river.

i18n.hi: रावर के नज़दीक या अरोड़ के पास, इतना तो सब मानते हैं, वहीं उनका सामना हुआ। चचनामा इस मैदाँ पर शकुनों और आग-भरे भाषणों की परत चढ़ाता है। इन्हें हटा दें तो भी सादा हक़ीक़त बचती है: एक ही नदी पर क़ाबू के लिए दो रियासतें।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-wide showing battle lines in motion without gore
panels.action: Elephants advance slowly, dust swirling around their feet, as Arab cavalry wheel to the flanks; banners strain in the wind, and both sides’ commanders watch from slightly raised positions.

dialogue.text: No eyewitness record survives of each charge and feint. Later writers gave us vivid duels. The more cautious historians see strategy: elephants to break ranks, cavalry to turn flanks, and commanders probing weaknesses.

i18n.hi: हर धावे और चाल का कोई आंखों देखा ब्यौरा नहीं बचा। बाद के लेखकों ने हमें रंगीन एकल-जंगें दीं। ज़्यादा एहतियात से लिखने वाले बस चालें देखते हैं: क़तारें तोड़ने को हाथी, पंखों से पलटवार को घुड़सवार, और सरदार जो हर कमज़ोरी टटोलते हैं।

panels.shot: medium on Raja Dahir atop an elephant amid the chaos
panels.action: Raja Dahir stands on the howdah of a war elephant, gripping a spear, his face strained yet resolute as the ordered lines around him waver, riders and footmen pulling back in confusion.

dialogue.text: Chachnama paints Dahir as a tragic hero, standing firm as allies falter. Whatever its embellishments, his end on that field marked the fall of a dynasty that had ruled Sindh for decades.

i18n.hi: चचनामा दाहिर को दुखांत नायक की तरह दिखाता है, जो साथ छोड़ते जाने पर भी डटा रहता है। बढ़ा-चढ़ा कर हो या नहीं, उस मैदाँ पर उसका अंजाम उस ख़ानदान का ढह जाना था जिसने सिंध पर कई दशकों तक राज किया।

panels.shot: muted wide of the battlefield aftermath, with distant view of Aror
panels.action: The field lies quiet under a hazy sky, scattered with abandoned standards, toppled equipment and riderless horses; in the distance, the citadel of Aror rises above the river bend.

dialogue.text: At Brahmanabad the chronicles record a massacre of the defenders, the numbers disputed, then a settlement: temples left standing under the tax, and Brahmin officials restored to run the province.

panels.shot: wide shot of Muhammad bin Qasim entering a city, greeted by mixed groups
panels.action: Muhammad bin Qasim rides into a Sindhi city gate, flanked by his guard, while some local notables step forward cautiously, hands raised in greeting, and townspeople look on with a mix of fear and curiosity.

dialogue.text: From Debal to Aror, al-Baladhuri records the new order: plunder and captives sent to Hajjaj, garrisons planted, the jizya fixed, and local elites who submitted left in place to collect it.

panels.shot: medium interior of a bureaucratic setting, scribes at work
panels.action: Inside a large hall, Arab and local scribes sit together, writing on parchment and palm leaves, while tax registers and maps of districts lie open; a commander and a local official confer over them.

dialogue.text: Sindh did not become an Arab heartland; it became a province. Garrison towns rose, stipends were assigned, and local elites who accepted the new order kept lands and offices in return for tribute to Iraq.

i18n.hi: सिंध किसी अरब दिल-ए-नग़र नहीं बना; वो एक सूबा बना। फ़ौजी क़स्बे खड़े हुए, ओझरों की तनख़्वाहें लिखी गईं, और जो देसी उमरा नए निज़ाम को मान गए, उन्होंने ज़मीनें और ओहदे रखे, बदले में इराक को ख़िराज दिया।

panels.shot: wide shot of ships at an Indus port now under Arab banners
panels.action: Ships load goods at a busy Indus port flying Arab banners, while Indian merchants barter on the quay, and distant warehouses and minaret-like watchtowers hint at new oversight of trade.

dialogue.text: This was the era pivot: Sindh’s ports and river routes now fed an imperial network stretching to Damascus and then Baghdad. Taxes, grain, and sometimes troops flowed, tying the Indus to the wider caliphate.

i18n.hi: ये वही मोड़ का ज़माना था: सिंध के बंदर और नदी-रास्ते अब एक ऐसे साम्राज्यी जाल को खिलाते थे जो दमिश्क से बग़दाद तक खिंचा था। कर, अनाज, और कभी-कभी सिपाही बहते रहे, सिंधु को पूरे ख़िलाफ़त से जोड़ते हुए।

panels.shot: intimate medium of a 13th-century scribe composing the Chachnama
panels.action: Centuries later, a Persian scribe in Sindh, Ali Kufi, sits by a lamp, writing on a manuscript as he looks out at a river town below, his face thoughtful, old texts and notes piled beside him.

dialogue.text: Five centuries later, Ali Kufi shaped these memories into the Chachnama. He wove courtly speeches, moral lessons and local pride into an old conquest, speaking as much to his own 13th-century Sindh as to 711.

i18n.hi: पांच सदियाँ बाद, अली कूफ़ी ने इन्हीं यादों को चचनामा की शक्ल दी। उसने दरबारी ख़ुत्बे, नैतिक सबक और स्थानीय शान को पुरानी फ़तह के साथ बुन दिया, उतना ही अपने १३वीं सदी के सिंध से बात करते हुए जितना ७११ से।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from a contemporary view of the Indus, fading into past scenes
panels.action: The modern Indus glides under a pale sky, boats moving slowly; ghostly overlays hint at old forts, banners and bustling markets that once lined its banks, fading in and out of the present.

dialogue.text: Dahir fell defending his river; within years a new caliph recalled bin Qasim, who died in his own sovereign's prison. The record holds conquest, tribute, slaughter and settlement alike. What it means, weigh for yourself.
